scenario: A mining company staffs emergency rescue teams with personnel who demonstrate advanced gas-detection skill OR expert confined-space navigation. The competencies are independent in the workforce pool; OR-gate selection creates apparent negative correlation among rescue team members.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (gas-detection skill) OR (confined-space navigation)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(gas_detection | ¬confined_nav, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(gas_detection | confined_nav, selected) and show it equals P(gas_detection). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between gas-detection skill and confined-space navigation.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks confined-space navigation must possess gas-detection skill to be admitted — hence P(gas_detection|¬confined_nav,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has confined-space navigation is admitted regardless of gas-detection skill, so P(gas_detection|confined_nav,sel)=P(gas_detection)=0.36. The gap (1.0 vs 0.36) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between gas-detection skill and confined-space navigation observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.36+0.54-0.36×0.54=0.7056. (2) Among candidates without confined-space navigation: only those with gas-detection skill are selected → P(gas_detection|¬confined_nav,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with confined-space navigation: selected regardless of gas-detection skill → P(gas_detection|confined_nav,sel)=P(gas_detection)=0.36. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬confined_nav raises P(gas_detection) from 0.36 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.36,0.54
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.7056)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.36)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
